title: Finiteness of Stein fibres and their residue fields for algebraic spaces
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$ a scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum], and $f:X\to T$ a proper morphism from an algebraic space [def-trf-algebraic-space, def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. Put $B=\Gamma(X_{\mathrm{et}},\mathcal O_X)$, the ring of global sections of the small etale structure sheaf, with its $A$-algebra structure given by pullback, and let $\pi:\operatorname{Spec}B\to T$ be the induced scheme map. For every $t\in T$, the point inverse image $\pi^{-1}(\{t\})$ is finite. For every $z$ in that inverse image the residue field extension $\kappa(z)/\kappa(t)$ is finite-dimensional [def-weil-residue-field, def-pc-field-extension]. Point spaces have the atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. No Noetherian hypothesis on $A$, flatness, finite-presentation or reducedness hypothesis on $f$, or scheme-representability hypothesis on $X$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0E1C, lemma-stein-universally-closed-residue-fields, specialized to proper f; the construction is Tag 0A19, lemma-stein-universally-closed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-stein-factorization-affine] to the given proper $f$. Its evaluation map $q:X\to Z=\operatorname{Spec}B$ satisfies $f=\pi q$, its ring map $A\to B$ is integral, and every fibre over $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(z)\to Z$ is nonempty. In particular $|q|$ is surjective: a field-valued point of this fibre represents a point of $X$ mapping to $z$. Only these clauses of the factorization node are used; geometric connectedness is not needed.

source.place: Tag 0E1C, lemma-stein-universally-closed-residue-fields, first two sentences; integral surjective factor from Tag 0A19, lemma-stein-universally-closed (available in the existing stronger Tag 0A1C node).

proof.text: Fix $t\in T$, put $k=\kappa(t)$ and $C=\pi^{-1}(\{t\})\subseteq|Z|$. The points of $Z$ are primes of $B$, and $\pi$ sends a prime to its inverse image in $A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-incomparability], distinct primes in $C$ cannot contain each other. In the Zariski topology a prime $\mathfrak q\,\!{}^\prime$ lies in $\overline{\{\mathfrak q\}}=V(\mathfrak q)$ exactly when $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak q\,\!{}^\prime$. Consequently $V(\mathfrak q)\cap C=\{\mathfrak q\}$ for every $\mathfrak q\in C$; in particular there are no distinct points of $C$ related by specialization.

source.place: Tag 0E1C, first sentence of proof; Algebra Tag 00GT, lemma-integral-no-inclusion.

proof.text: Form $X_t=X\times_T\operatorname{Spec}k$, which is an algebraic space by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Properness includes finite type [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. Base-change stability in [lem-sfb-stack-finite-type-calculus], whose statement explicitly agrees with the ordinary algebraic-space notion, makes $X_t\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ finite type. Its quasi-compactness, tested on the quasi-compact scheme $\operatorname{Spec}k$, says that $X_t$ admits a surjective etale map from a quasi-compact scheme; by the last clause of [lem-a1-space-finite-affine-subatlas] its point space $|X_t|$ is quasi-compact. The map $X_t\to X\xrightarrow q Z$ has image exactly $C$: one inclusion follows from $f=\pi q$; for the other, choose $x\in|X|$ mapping to $z\in C$ by step 1, and apply the point-fibre-product surjectivity of [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus] to $X\to T\leftarrow\operatorname{Spec}k$. It supplies a point of $X_t$ projecting to $x$, hence mapping to $z$. Every point map used here is continuous by the same node.

source.place: Tag 0E1C, proof: surjection from the fibre and its finite type; Properties of Spaces Tag 03H4, lemma-points-cartesian; Stacks Morphisms Tag 06FU, lemma-base-change-finite-type.

proof.text: Choose a scheme atlas of $X_t$ as in [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Refine it to a disjoint union of affine schemes by [lem-a1-space-atlas-open-refinement-pullback]. Apply [lem-a1-space-finite-affine-subatlas] to the quasi-compact point space from step 3. This gives finitely many affine schemes $U_j=\operatorname{Spec}R_j$ whose coproduct maps to $X_t$ by a representable surjective etale map; by [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus] this map is surjective on points, so the maps $|U_j|\to|X_t|$ are jointly surjective. Composing with $X_t\to Z$ gives scheme morphisms $h_j:U_j\to Z$, since a map between representable sheaves is the corresponding scheme map. Their point images cover $C$, by step 3. The chart test of [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties], with target chart the identity of $\operatorname{Spec}k$, makes each $U_j\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ locally of finite type.

source.place: Tag 0E1C, Noetherian fibre sentence, expanded on finite affine charts; Properties of Spaces Tags 03FX, lemma-cover-by-union-affines, and 03E4, lemma-quasi-compact-space.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs], $R_j$ is a finitely generated $k$-algebra. The field $k$ is Noetherian: a nonzero ideal contains an invertible element and hence $1$, so its only ideals are $(0)$ and $(1)$. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] makes $R_j$ Noetherian. The single affine open $U_j$ satisfies [pqf-def-locnoeth], and $U_j$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]; thus it is a Noetherian scheme. Applying [lem-sc-noetherian-closed-subset-finite-components] to the closed subset $E=U_j$ writes $U_j$ as a finite union of irreducible components. By [lem-sc-scheme-sober] each nonempty component has a generic point $\eta_{j,a}$. There are only finitely many such generic points over all $j$, and every $u\in U_j$ lies in $\overline{\{\eta_{j,a}\}}$ for at least one $a$.

source.place: Tag 0E1C, Noetherian fibre sentence and omitted topological argument, expanded via affine charts; Algebra Tag 00FN, lemma-Noetherian-permanence; Properties Tag 0BA8, lemma-Noetherian-irreducible-components; Schemes Tag 01IS, lemma-scheme-sober.

proof.text: For $z\in C$, choose $j$ and $u\in U_j$ with $h_j(u)=z$ (step 4), then choose $\eta_{j,a}$ specializing to $u$ (step 5). Continuity of the scheme map $h_j$ gives $h_j(u)\in\overline{\{h_j(\eta_{j,a})\}}$. Both points belong to $C$, so step 2 forces $z=h_j(\eta_{j,a})$. Thus $C$ is contained in the image of the finite set of generic points from step 5. The reverse containment follows because each chart maps into $C$. Hence $C$ is finite. This supplies the topological argument omitted in Tag 0E1C: it uses generic points of the scheme charts and never assumes that an arbitrary Noetherian topological space is sober.

source.place: Tag 0E1C, proof, sentence “A topological argument (omitted) now shows ...”, explicitly filled using steps 2--5.

proof.text: Now fix $z\in C$ and choose a chart $h_j$ whose image contains $z$. Write $\mathfrak q_z$ for the prime of $B$ corresponding to $z$. The subset $E_j=h_j^{-1}(V(\mathfrak q_z))$ is closed in $U_j$, and by step 2 and $h_j(U_j)\subseteq C$ it equals $h_j^{-1}(\{z\})$; it is nonempty. By [lem-sfb-finite-type-points-detect-open], choose a finite type point $u\in E_j$, meaning that $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)\to U_j$ is of finite type. Composing it with the locally finite type scheme map $U_j\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally of finite type by clause (e) of [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence]. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-type-field-point-characterization] to this composite. Since the target is the one-point scheme $\operatorname{Spec}k$, it gives $[\kappa(u):k]<\infty$. This uses a finite type point in a closed subset of an actual scheme chart, so no assumption about closed rational points or representability of $X$ is made.

source.place: Tag 0E1C, proof, choice of a finite type point and field-finiteness argument; scheme-chart version using Morphisms Tags 02J4, lemma-enough-finite-type-points, 01T3, lemma-composition-finite-type, and 01TA, lemma-point-finite-type.

proof.text: The scheme morphism $h_j$ induces an embedding $\kappa(z)\hookrightarrow\kappa(u)$ on residue fields [def-weil-residue-field]. It is an embedding over $k=\kappa(t)$: the maps $U_j\to Z\to T$ and $U_j\to\operatorname{Spec}k\to T$ agree, so their local-ring maps and residue maps agree; the latter factors through the canonical residue map at $t$. Regard $\kappa(z)$ as a $k$-linear subspace of $\kappa(u)$. Any $k$-linearly independent family in it remains independent under the injection, hence has size at most $\dim_k\kappa(u)$, which is finite by step 7. Therefore $[\kappa(z):\kappa(t)]<\infty$. If $C$ is empty there is no $z$ to treat; if $X$ is empty the atlas and the finite sets above can all be empty. The argument only used Noetherianity of finite type algebras over $k$, and imposed no Noetherian, reducedness, flatness or finite-presentation hypothesis on the original base or morphism.

source.place: Tag 0E1C, last sentence of proof: the intermediate residue-field extension is finite; linear-independence argument written out.
